title: Cheat Sheet - Algorithms
markdown:
## Growth rates

| Class | n = 10³ | n = 10⁶ | Rule of thumb for 1 second |
|---|---|---|---|
| O(1), O(log n) | 1, 10 | 1, 20 | any n |
| O(n) | 10³ | 10⁶ | n up to about 10⁸ |
| O(n log n) | 10⁴ | 2 × 10⁷ | n up to about 10⁷ |
| O(n²) | 10⁶ | 10¹² | n up to about 10⁴ |
| O(n³) | 10⁹ | 10¹⁸ | n up to about 500 |
| O(2ⁿ) | - | - | n up to about 25 |
| O(n!) | - | - | n up to about 11 |

## Containers

| Container | Access | Search | Insert / erase | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `std::vector` | O(1) | O(n) | O(1)* at end, O(n) elsewhere | the default |
| `std::deque` | O(1) | O(n) | O(1) at both ends | queues |
| `std::list` | - | O(n) | O(1) at a known node | splice, stable addresses |
| `std::set` / `std::map` | - | O(log n) | O(log n) | sorted; red-black tree |
| `std::unordered_set` / `_map` | - | O(1) avg | O(1) avg | hash table; worst case O(n) |
| `std::priority_queue` | top O(1) | - | O(log n) | max-heap; `std::greater` for min |
| sorted `std::vector` | O(1) | O(log n) | O(n) | best for static data |

\* amortised

## Sorting

| Sort | Average | Worst | Space | Stable |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| insertion | n² | n² | 1 | yes |
| merge (`std::stable_sort`) | n log n | n log n | n | yes |
| quick | n log n | n² | log n | no |
| heap | n log n | n log n | 1 | no |
| introsort (`std::sort`) | n log n | n log n | log n | no |
| counting | n + k | n + k | n + k | yes |
| radix (LSD) | d(n + b) | d(n + b) | n + b | yes |

```cpp-norun
std::sort(v.begin(), v.end());                                         // ascending
std::sort(v.begin(), v.end(), std::greater<>());                       // descending
std::sort(v.begin(), v.end(), [](const P& a, const P& b) { return std::tie(a.age, a.name) < std::tie(b.age, b.name); });
std::stable_sort(v.begin(), v.end(), cmp);                             // keeps equal elements in order
std::nth_element(v.begin(), v.begin() + k, v.end());                   // k-th smallest at position k, O(n)
std::partial_sort(v.begin(), v.begin() + k, v.end());                  // the k smallest, sorted
```

## Binary search

```cpp-norun
std::size_t lo = 0, hi = a.size();              // answer in [lo, hi]
while (lo < hi)
{
    std::size_t mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
    if (a[mid] < x) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid; // first index with a[i] >= x
}
// on the answer: smallest x with ok(x), when ok is false...false true...true
while (lo < hi) { auto mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2; if (ok(mid)) hi = mid; else lo = mid + 1; }
```

`std::lower_bound` (first ≥), `std::upper_bound` (first >), `std::equal_range`, `std::binary_search`.

## Heaps

```cpp-norun
std::priority_queue<int> maxHeap;
std::priority_queue<int, std::vector<int>, std::greater<int>> minHeap;
// array layout: children of i at 2i + 1 and 2i + 2, parent at (i - 1) / 2
```

Top k of a stream: min-heap of size k. k-way merge: min-heap of (value, list, index). Running median: max-heap of the lower half + min-heap of the upper half.

## Trees

| Structure | Operations | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| BST (unbalanced) | search, insert, erase | O(h), h up to n |
| AVL / red-black | search, insert, erase, floor, ceiling | O(log n) |
| + subtree sizes | rank, select | O(log n) |
| Fenwick tree | point add, prefix sum | O(log n) |
| segment tree | point update, range min/max/sum | O(log n) |
| union-find | find, unite | O(α(n)) ≈ O(1) |
| trie | insert, find, prefix count | O(length) |

```cpp-norun
// Fenwick (1-based): lowbit = i & -i
for (; i <= n; i += i & -i) t[i] += delta;      // add
for (; i > 0; i -= i & -i) s += t[i];           // prefix sum
```

## Graphs

| Problem | Algorithm | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| fewest edges | BFS | O(V + E) |
| reachability, components | BFS / DFS / union-find | O(V + E) |
| cycle in a directed graph | DFS with three colours | O(V + E) |
| dependency order | topological sort (Kahn or DFS) | O(V + E) |
| shortest paths, weights ≥ 0 | Dijkstra with a heap | O((V + E) log V) |
| weights 0 or 1 | 0-1 BFS with a deque | O(V + E) |
| negative weights | Bellman-Ford | O(VE) |
| all pairs, small V | Floyd-Warshall | O(V³) |
| one target on a map | A* with an admissible heuristic | ≤ Dijkstra |
| cheapest connecting network | Kruskal (sort + union-find) or Prim (heap) | O(E log E) |

```cpp-norun
// Dijkstra with lazy deletion
std::priority_queue<std::pair<long long, int>, std::vector<std::pair<long long, int>>, std::greater<>> pq;
dist[s] = 0; pq.push({ 0, s });
while (!pq.empty())
{
    auto [d, u] = pq.top(); pq.pop();
    if (d > dist[u]) continue;
    for (auto [v, w] : adj[u])
        if (d + w < dist[v]) { dist[v] = d + w; pq.push({ dist[v], v }); }
}
```

## Algorithm design

| Technique | Use when | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| two pointers / sliding window | sorted data or contiguous ranges | pair sum, window maximum |
| binary search on the answer | "smallest x that works", monotonic check | shipping capacity, eating speed |
| greedy | a provably safe local choice exists | interval scheduling, Huffman, MST |
| divide and conquer | independent halves combine cheaply | merge sort, counting inversions |
| dynamic programming | overlapping subproblems, optimal substructure | knapsack, LCS, edit distance, coin change |
| backtracking | search with strong pruning | N queens, Sudoku, subsets |

DP recipe: **state**, **transition**, **base cases**, **order**; store choices to rebuild the answer.
